summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman with end-stage renal disease, type 1 diabetes, and a history of bilateral lower extremity amputations was admitted for nausea and vomiting after taking Nyquil, along with a new nonproductive cough. She was found to have leukocytosis and a positive blood culture for Staphylococcus epidermidis, prompting evaluation for bacteremia. A tunneled hemodialysis catheter was lost on hospital day two, requiring temporary peritoneal dialysis, which she did not tolerate. After 24 hours of negative blood cultures, a new tunneled catheter was placed, and IV vancomycin was resumed. Infectious disease recommended a two-week course of vancomycin despite the likely contaminant, and transesophageal echocardiogram ruled out endocarditis. Urine culture grew E. coli, but due to lack of symptoms, it was deemed colonization and not treated. Her cough improved with bronchodilators and resolved by discharge. She was discharged home with services to complete vancomycin during dialysis and follow up with her care team.
